AN ORDINANCE OF THE MAYOR AND COUNCIL OF THE TOWN OF PINE MOUNTAIN, GEORGIA (“TOWN”), TO ADOPT RULES AND REGULATIONS FOR FOG TRAPS AND INTERCEPTORS

BE IT ORDAINED that the Town of Pine Mountain hereby adopts the following Ordinance to ensure compliance with existing federal, state, and local law with respect to fats, oils, and greases (“FOG”) traps/interceptors and to prevent excessive FOG from entering the Town of Pine Mountain Sewer System.

- (a) Purpose. The intent of this ordinance is to ensure compliance with the rules and regulations set forth by existing federal, state and local law and to provide specific standards for fats, oils, and greases (“FOG”) traps/interceptors location, type, size, construction, installation, and maintenance, to prevent excessive FOG from entering the Town of Pine Mountain sewer system. In accordance with this ordinance and other applicable law, food service establishments, which shall have the meaning set forth in O.C.G.A. § 26-2-370(2), shall provide means of preventing FOG discharges into the sanitary sewer system by installing and maintaining traps/interceptors at the owner, leaseholder, or operator's expense using the guidelines set forth in this ordinance. Failure to comply may result in penalties as set forth in this ordinance.

- (b) General requirements. The following design, administrative, operational, and other requirements are applicable to all food service establishments. Specific requirements for FOG trap/interceptor construction for both new and existing food service establishments can be found in subsection (g) of this ordinance.

- (1) All food service establishments shall have FOG-handling systems approved by the Town of Pine Mountain. Existing establishments whose FOG-handling facilities are not in accordance with this ordinance shall install approved devices within 90 days from adoption of this ordinance.

- (2) All food service establishment operations shall be subject to periodic review, evaluation, and inspection by the Town of Pine Mountain or its designated agent.

- (3) Violations of the FOG standards set forth in this ordinance may result in enforcement actions as outlined in this ordinance.

- (4) Food service establishments whose operations cause or allow excessive FOG to discharge or accumulate in the sewer collection system may be liable for all costs associated with line blockages, line cleaning, line repair where

needed, any stop-ups or overflows, and any damage to public or private property that is a direct result of or proximately related to FOG accumulation related to the food service establishment in violation.

- (5) All traps/interceptors shall be designed and installed in accordance with this ordinance.

- (6) All food service establishments must complete a permit application for the discharge of waste from food preparation and food service industries into the

Town of Pine Mountain sewer system.

- (c) Inspection and sampling. The Town of Pine Mountain may inspect the facility of any user to determine compliance with this ordinance. Facilities where wastewater is created or discharged shall allow the Town of Pine Mountain’s representatives ready access at all reasonable times to all parts of the premises for the purpose of inspection. Unreasonable delays and/or denial of access shall be in direct violation of this ordinance, and be subject to the penalties as set forth in this ordinance.

An applicant for the installation of an approved device shall notify the Public Works Superintendent of the Town of Pine Mountain before any backfill, and when the device is ready for inspection and connection to the public sewer. The connection shall be made under the supervision of the Superintendent of Public

Works of the Town of Pine Mountain or his or her designated representative.

- (1) In-ground devices. Food service establishments with these devices shall adhere to a clean-out maintenance schedule as required by the Town of Pine Mountain. Schedules will be set using the following criteria: business operating hours, seating capacity, types of food service provided, size of device, and inspection results.

- (2) General installation requirements.

- a. FOG traps shall be installed as close to the source of FOG as possible, or so installed to allow the waste stream to cool considerably before entering the trap system.

-7-

The FOG trap shall either be baffled to retain congealed FOG on the surface of the liquid or contain two chambers for primary and secondary settling.

Influent shall enter the trap a minimum of six inches below the normal liquid level to keep the surface as still as possible.

Effluent shall be drawn from near the bottom of the trap at a minimum of 18 inches below the liquid level.

Inlet and outlet of trap shall be provided with clean-outs for unplugging both sewers and dip pipes. Food waste disposers may not be connected through a FOG interceptor.

A large manhole, removable slab, or other cover to suit traffic load shall be installed so that all chambers of the trap are readily accessible for complete cleaning of both floatable and settleable solids. Top or cover shall be gas tight.

FOG collected from an interceptor shall not be introduced into any drainage piping, public or private sewer.

Sanitary/domestic waste shall not be allowed to flow in any interceptor/trap system.

- k. All traps/interceptors shall have installed a means to prevent the introduction of materials into the pretreatment system such as paper, plastics, metals or other materials that which if introduced into the sanitary sewer system or directly into the headworks of any Publicly Owned Treatment Works(“POTW”), will cause obstruction, interference or damage to any of the conveyance systems or POTW.

- 1. The following criteria will be used to determine the sufficiency of trap size: (i) Class code; (ii) Hours of operation; and (iii) Seating capacity.

- (i) In-ground devices. Sizes shall be determined using the criteria listed above, and capacity standards as listed in subsection (g)(1) of this ordinance.

- (ii) All devices must have approval from the Town of Pine Mountain prior to construction or installation, and adhere to any local and/or state plumbing codes that may apply.

- (3) New food service establishments. All food service establishments applying for water/sewer service shall be required to submit plans and/or drawings outlining the plumbing layout and location of the required in-ground FOG trap installation.

- (h) FOG enforcement. The Town of Pine Mountain or its designated agent will conduct random inspections to ensure that proper maintenance and clean-out schedules are being followed.

Clean-out schedules may be set and/or modified by the Town of Pine Mountain. Clean-out frequency may increase or decrease depending on the efficiency (prevention of FOG entering the sewer system) of the device installed. Failure to comply with these schedules may subject the user/owner to the penalties as outlined in this ordinance.

Any facility that is found to be responsible for a sewer line blockage and/or sanitary sewer overflow will be liable for any expenses incurred from the cleanup or unstopping of the sewer line/system.

- (i) Other facilities. Other facilities beyond food service establishments that are required by the Town Council of the Town of Pine Mountain to discharge their waste stream into the Town of Pine Mountain sanitary sewer shall meet the following requirements:

- (1) An approved sand trap/interceptor must be installed and maintained for the prevention of sand, oil, and FOG from entering the sewer system.

- (2) Sand trap/interceptors shall be covered with an approved roof and devices in place to prevent storm water run-off from entering the sanitary sewer system.

- (j) Enforcement

The Town of Pine Mountain reserves the right to enforce the requirements set forth in this ordinance in any legal manner, including, without limitation, the following:

- (1) Emergency termination of service. In the event of an actual or threatened discharge to the POTW of any pollutant which presents an imminent and substantial danger to the health or safety of persons, or danger of interference with the POTW, the Town of Pine Mountain shall immediately notify the user or other person causing or responsible for the condition and request their assistance in abating the same. The Town of Pine Mountain may temporarily terminate service of such user or users to abate the condition when such action is reasonably necessary. Such service shall be restored by the Town of Pine Mountain as soon as the emergency situation has been abated or corrected.

- (2) Notification of violation. Any person found to be violating any provision of this ordinance shall be served by the Town of Pine Mountain with written

notice stating the nature of the violation and providing reasonable time limit for the satisfactory correction thereof. The user shall, within the period of time stated in such notice, permanently cease and/or remedy all violations.

- (3) Revocation of service. Any user who violates the conditions of this ordinance and/or applicable state and federal laws and/or regulations, is subject to revocation of his water and sewer service by the Town of Pine
